claim: The disclosed request was POST /stats/workouts/details with an ids array.
qualification: Keep this endpoint separate from the disclosure’s search and GraphQL issues.

claim: The web client populated the IDs; IDs visible in the mobile app could be manually substituted and sent.
qualification: The source demonstrates editable request IDs, not Peloton’s server implementation.

claim: The endpoint originally accepted unauthenticated requests.
evidence: “possible for unauthenticated users to make this request”
qualification: State only what the researcher observed.

claim: The partial fix required an account but still exposed the same data to other Peloton users.
evidence: “user data was now only available to all authenticated Peloton users”
qualification: This is the decisive cross-member object-authorization evidence.

claim: The workout response disclosed personal data even for profiles set to private.
evidence: “Personal data disclosed, despite profile being set as ‘private’”
qualification: The screenshots carry some detail; do not invent fields absent from the text or image.

claim: The researcher disclosed on 20 January 2021 and recorded the partial fix on 2 February 2021.
evidence: “unauthenticated API endpoint issue was silently and partly resolved”

claim: The 5 May 2021 update says the vulnerabilities were largely fixed within seven days after press contact.
evidence: “The vulnerabilities were largely fixed within 7 days.”
qualification: “Largely” matters; do not upgrade it to a complete fix.
